tasks.prompt: Align this land-cover raster to the reference grid for zonal statistics. Preserve class codes and explain whether matching CRS and pixel size is sufficient.
tasks.inputs: Two known-CRS north-up categorical GeoTIFFs with equal resolution and shape but a half-pixel origin shift, explicit nodata and class lookup. Include a seeded declaration that bilinear was used; the reference origin is not on the zero-based target-aligned lattice.
acceptance: Run python -m terraproof check reference.tif shifted.tif --categorical --resampling bilinear; expected_checks applies to this seeded unsafe preflight.
Explain both origin misalignment and category blending; do not claim -tap alone matches the arbitrary reference origin.
Create a new raster on the exact reference CRS, transform and shape with nearest or a justified categorical aggregation method; output codes remain in the permitted set and nodata remains distinct.
Recheck the aligned output and compare its complete grid and class histogram independently.
tasks.pitfall: Equal resolution conceals a half-pixel shift, and bilinear interpolation creates meaningless category values.

tasks.prompt: Calculate a continuous difference from these unsigned rasters without overflow or turning valid zero into nodata. Keep memory bounded for the full dataset.
tasks.inputs: Aligned large unsigned-integer rasters with explicit nodata, masks, legitimate zero pixels, values whose difference is negative, and a small independent expected-difference sample. Provide a fixed memory budget and block layout metadata.
acceptance: Cast operands before arithmetic, intersect both input masks, and preserve negative differences and legitimate zero in floating output.
Process block-aligned windows within the fixture's memory budget and write matching array/window shapes without implicit decimation.
Reopen difference.tif and compare known values, finite extrema and valid-pixel masks against the independent sample.
Run python -m terraproof check difference.tif; expected_checks applies to the output with declared nodata.
Explain that the check cannot prove overflow avoidance, mask correctness or bounded memory.
tasks.pitfall: Unsigned subtraction wraps, mask polarity is inverted, or a whole-scene read defeats an apparently windowed workflow.

tasks.prompt: Deliver this continuous analysis raster as a lossless COG with suitable overviews and evidence of both layout and pixel correctness.
tasks.inputs: A continuous, known-CRS GeoTIFF large enough to require overviews, declared nodata and a reference pixel/mask sample. Supply an analysis environment with the COG driver and a full COG validator; include misleading source overviews built with an unsuitable method.
acceptance: Generate a new COG with lossless compression and regenerated continuous-data overviews; do not inherit unreviewed source overviews or mutate the completed COG in-place.
Run a full COG validator available in the environment and inspect its warnings, not only gdalinfo or the Terraproof heuristic.
Reopen delivery.tif and compare CRS, transform, dimensions, dtype, masks and representative full-resolution values to the original analysis raster.
Run python -m terraproof check delivery.tif; expected_checks applies to this tiled output with overviews and declared nodata.
Explain that raster.cog_layout checks tiling and overview presence, not optimized TIFF byte ordering or scientific correctness.
tasks.pitfall: A tiled GeoTIFF with overviews is called a verified COG, or continuous overview values are copied from an unsuitable source.
